_doc: MABEL master control-law parameter registry — the single, human-editable surface for every controller hyperparameter in the `mabel` package (controller/mabel/). Gains, barriers, admittance masses, workspace boxes and safety limits ARE the control law; the hardware bridge only executes the motor commands that fall out of them, so they live here in controller/ (not in hardware_bridge/). Read by controller/mabel/control_params.py and consumers listed per block.

_source_legend.LIVE: This block is READ by running code today — editing the numbers here changes the robot's behaviour with no code change. Consumers are named in each block's `_consumers`.
_source_legend.MIRROR: Documentation copy of a value that is currently authoritative in controller/mabel/config.py or controller/mabel/motion_model/tip_over.py. Editing here does NOT yet change behaviour — edit the cited `_authoritative` source too (or wire the block up). Kept here so this file is the one place to READ every tunable; the migration to make these LIVE is tracked in docs/mabel_controller.tex (Config registry section).
_source_legend.PLACEHOLDER: The subsystem is not yet fully configured on the real robot; the numbers are conservative starting points or hardware defaults. Tune before relying on them.

arm._doc: The real-robot arm control law: DaMiao MIT torque law T = kp*(q*-q) + kd*(q̇*-q̇) + t_ff. Per-joint kp (N.m/rad) / kd (N.m.s/rad) / vmax (rad/s). kd is HARD-capped at the DaMiao MIT wire limit (kd_max ~5); kp is derived per-joint from the MJCF inertia so a heavy shoulder and a light wrist are not forced to share one gain — regenerate with the upstream arm stack --ff.

system_id._doc: Joint system identity — the firmware joint IDs, their MJCF joint names, the backend that speaks to them, and the per-side motor limits. This is the map every torque quantity is expressed against: q_model = model_mid + dir*(q_raw - raw_mid), and torque transforms the same way (tau_raw = dir*tau_model). The calibration `dir` and raw window are NOT duplicated here — they are measured by the setup studio and live in the CalibrationStore (calib_slice below) to avoid two diverging copies; this block is the naming + limit registry only.

gravity_feedforward._doc: t_ff = gravity torque g(q) from the MJCF (ORCA hand + wrist mount, ~1.74 kg per wrist when hands=orca). kd<=5 caps kp below what gravity needs, so t_ff is what HOLDS the arm up while kp only tracks. There is no per-joint FF gain — the feedforward IS the model gravity term; the tunables are the safety envelope + the hand-mass choice below.
gravity_feedforward._hands_note: 'none' (default) strips the ORCA hand subtree mass so the FF lifts the arm only — a phantom 1.12 kg/side makes the arm SHAKE if the hands are not bolted on. Set 'orca' once the hands are fitted.
gravity_feedforward._env_overrides: MABEL_ARMS_HANDS, MABEL_ARMS_FF_SCALE, MABEL_ARMS_MOUNT_TILT_DEG still override at runtime.
gravity_feedforward._sysid_2026_07_28: NO-HANDS sysid (exp_arm_gravity_sysid.py, 25 poses, PD holds): measured/model scale l_j4 +0.96, l_j2 +0.72, l_j1 +0.40 (J1 signal ~stiction, trimmed conservatively to 0.5); RMS 1.1-1.7 N*m = the stiction band; ALSO fixed dir(l_j3/l_j4) = -1 (replacement motors mirror-wound). Right-arm trims mirrored from left (same mechanics, unmeasured). hands:'none' = ORCA mass STRIPPED; set 'orca' when hands are refitted and RE-RUN the sysid with hands on before trusting these trims.
gravity_feedforward._sysid_2026_07_29: LIFT-ARC sysid v2 (27 poses through center height, stiff-identify + safe-lowering): MJCF(hands=none, mount_tilt 0) fits meas at scales l_j1 0.42 / l_j2 0.88 / l_j4 0.98, residual RMS 0.4-1.0 N*m (= stiction band). URDF independent theory agrees exactly (same |scales|, same residuals). tilt 0 CONFIRMED over +/-10 by the J2 fit — the MJCF's drawn -10 deg is corrected in-code and the metal is 0. Right arm mirrored, unmeasured. NO-HANDS variant; re-run with hands=orca when refitted.

soft_drag._doc: SOFT mode = POSITION-based drag-and-hold (operator design 2026-07-30, replacing the tau-observer admittance that went erratic live): nonzero P; while the user pushes (|q - target| > band AND |qd| > qd_min) the target follows the measured position, stopping band short; when the push stops the target FREEZES. No torque feedback in the loop = cannot self-excite; quasi-static gravity-residual sag stays below qd_min and is arrested by the kp*band spring. Read LIVE by controller/mabel/arm_control/drag_follow.py via control_params.arm_soft_drag().

soft_gains._doc: How the app's stiffness slider (control_mode.stiffness, 0..1) maps onto SOFT-mode PD gains, applied over the STIFF arm.gains set and shipped to the HAL on /arms/gains: kp_soft = kp_stiff * (kp_scale_min + (kp_scale_max - kp_scale_min) * stiffness); kd_soft = kd_stiff * kd_scale. STIFF mode always runs the arm.gains set unscaled.
soft_gains._scale_note_2026_07_30: Floor raised 0.25 -> 0.5 (operator: sim-soft holds perfectly because it is a TORQUE controller with a perfect model; real soft must HOLD with PD against the imperfect FF - sag = residual/kp, so kp 6 sagged ~14 deg on the worst joint). Softness on real comes from the drag-follow BEHAVIOR, not weak holding gains.

soft_float._doc: FLOATING soft mode (admittance): tau_ext = tau_g_model(q) - tau_meas -> per-joint virtual mass-damper -> streamed position targets, so a dragged arm FLOATS and parks where released instead of rubber-banding against kp. The AUTO-TARE bias absorbs the gravity-model residual at every rest pose (entry tare + rate-limited re-tare while quiet), which is what keeps floating honest despite the imperfect real-robot mass/CoM sysid; the deadbands then only cover residual VARIATION (measured band RMS 0.4-1.0 N*m, sysid v2 2026-07-29) and stay small enough to feel floaty. Read LIVE by controller/mabel/arm_control/admittance.py via control_params.arm_soft_float(); keys mirror FLOAT_DEFAULTS (per-class j1..j7).

impedance._doc: Soft/compliant arm mode: scales the stiff PD gains down and floors the damping so the arm yields to contact.

rate_limit._doc: Real-only per-joint velocity slew limit (sim poses instantly). Caps how fast a commanded joint target may move so a slider slam does not become a 99 N.m step.

gains_pd_candidate._doc: DERIVED candidate PD gains for the real arm, 2026-08-23. NOT LIVE and NOT APPLIED: arm.gains above is the deliberately COMPLIANT set from 2026-07-29 ('as compliant as possible', gravity FF carries the load), and changing real-arm stiffness is a hardware decision that needs an on-robot ramp with the operator present. This block records what the same derivation used for the sim (kp_j = M_j w^2, kd_j = 2 zeta M_j w, M_j measured off the MJCF) asks for on hardware, and what the CURRENT gains actually give, so the trade is visible without re-deriving it. See controller/docs/arm_pd_tuning.tex and experiments/exp_pd_tuning.py.
gains_pd_candidate._constraint: The DaMiao MIT wire caps kd at ~5 N.m.s/rad. With kd capped, tracking lag (kd/kp) and damping ratio (kd / 2 sqrt(kp M)) trade DIRECTLY: zeta = 0.5*sqrt(kd*L/M) for a target lag L. That is why the real arm cannot reach the sim's 32 ms lag at zeta = 1, and why the velocity feedforward already on the wire (ros_plant._js -> _arm_target_velocity) matters more than the gains: it cancels the kd*(0 - dq) term that the lag comes from.

_design.inertia_source: MJCF median reflected inertia, exp_pd_tuning.py P1

position_control._doc: Day-1 pure PD (sim torque path). kp/kd default to 'servo' — inherited PER JOINT from the MuJoCo actuator gainprm/biasprm, NOT a scalar; the real-robot per-joint numbers are arm.gains above. tau_limit inherits each actuator's |forcerange|; joints with no forcerange fall back to tau_fallback.

gravity_compensation._doc: WBC-region gravity/bias feedforward for the sim torque runtime (distinct from arm.gravity_feedforward, which is the real-robot raw-frame arm law). Cancels g(q) so only a light joint damper remains; the operator/IK then commands motion against near-zero gravity load.

collision_avoidance._authoritative: controller/mabel/config.py (SC_* constants); read via None-fallback by controller/mabel/whole_body_controller/collision_avoidance/capsule_guard.py
collision_avoidance._doc: Capsule self-collision guard — the SOLE arm-arm defense (the MJCF disables arm-arm contacts). ON by default. Two laws: 'stop' = Faverjon-Tournassoud velocity damper (decelerate to a stop AT the margin along the intended path — feels like a wall); 'cbf' = tracking-QP with a control barrier (slides around obstacles — 'force field' feel). alpha is the control-barrier gain: allowed approach rate ḋ >= -alpha*(d - margin). The torque-domain 'soft wall' (barrier_kv/kp) brakes closing velocity and springs back out when a dragged arm reaches the margin.

admittance._authoritative: controller/mabel/config.py (ADMIT_*, DRAG_*); read via None-fallback by controller/mabel/whole_body_controller/admittance/base_admittance.py
admittance._doc: Whole-body force compliance: the base behaves as a virtual planar mass with viscous + Coulomb 'virtual friction' driven by the external drag wrench, so an operator can push the robot around by the arm. A small comfort box (drag_box, referenced to the neutral hand pose) makes the base engage quickly so the arm never reaches its limit and tips the body. NOTE: WBCEngine constructs BaseAdmittance with the two engine_overrides below instead of the config defaults.

engine_overrides._doc: controller/mabel/whole_body_controller/engine.py builds BaseAdmittance(ang_damping=7.0, m_static=2.5) — a one-hand push then yaws more freely than the standalone config default.

wrench_estimation._doc: External-wrench estimation + contact localization feeding the admittance base. lam is the DLS regularizer on the Jacobian pseudo-inverse; gain is the momentum-observer bandwidth; confirm/hold debounce a contact before it is trusted.

compliance._doc: Region-selectable compliance runtime. compliant_damping is the residual joint damper left after gravity cancellation (low = soft); lazy_damping holds the slow torso/lift joints. The workspace_box below is what makes the MOBILE BASE move: when the hand centroid leaves this comfort box (robot-local frame, chassis-centre origin), the lazy base follower translates/yaws so the arms never reach their kinematic limit and pull the body over.

workspace_box._doc: Hand-centroid comfort box in the robot frame. e_fwd is measured from the chassis centre (under the torso), so e_fwd==0 is the body line; the base retreats the instant a wrist crosses behind the torso. drag_box is the tighter force-compliance box (hand excursion from neutral before the base follows).

whole_body_ik._doc: Bimanual SE(3) differential IK — weighted damped-least-squares with null-space posture. kp_pos/kp_rot are the end-effector task gains; damping is the DLS lambda; posture_gain pulls the null space toward the rest pose; weight_lift/torso make those DOFs 'lazy' (higher = the solver uses them less). Deadbands ignore sub-threshold EE error so the arm does not chase gravity sag.

base._authoritative: controller/mabel/motion_model/tip_over.py (re-exported by config.py) + config.py (WHEEL_RADIUS, STEER_DEADBAND, MODULE_*, NAV_*); hardware_bridge/mabel_hw/config.py (BASE)
base._doc: 3-module delta swerve base. Every base twist MUST pass through config.safe_base_step(...) (the tip-over ZMP limiter) BEFORE swerve_ik — a raw hard-stop or turn-while-driving can tip the robot. The tip-over constants (levers, CoM, safety factors, stop times) are MEASURED from the chassis support polygon and re-derived from the MJCF by experiments/wbc_stability.py (E4); re-measure on any mass/geometry change.

tip_over._doc: MJCF-measured; do not hand-tune without re-running experiments/wbc_stability.py (E4). tip_lever_* are the horizontal distances from the CoM ground-projection to each support edge; tip_sf_* are safety factors; stop_time_* are the assumed decel windows; com_* are the CoM height model (z0 + dz/dlift * lift).

navigation._doc: Drone-style virtual joysticks (apps navigation mode). Full-deflection magnitudes.

hardware._doc: Base hardware limits from hardware_bridge/mabel_hw/config.py (BASE). drive_gain is pinned at 1.0: the SPARK drive velocity loop under-reaches to ~50% of commanded (kF=0) and COLLAPSES above ~1.5 m/s — the real fix is the SPARK kFF + current limit in REV Hardware Client, not this gain.

neck._doc: 3-DOF neck look-at (decoupled from the body). kp is the pointing gain; the gaze ray starts ray_offset ahead of the head to clear the body, uses fallback_dist when no scene hit is found, and treats hits closer than min_hit_dist as self-hits.

hardware._doc: DaMiao neck (yaw/pitch/roll), MIT mode, shares the arms' DaMiao protocol. Motor map + torque are configured in hardware_bridge/mabel_hw/config.py (BODY); the neck is not yet fully brought up (BODY enabled=false by default).

hands._doc: ORCA hands (position control, decoupled from the body). The finger-joint servo kp/kd live in the MJCF (position-servo actuators) — the retargeter only writes ctrl TARGETS, so there is no Python PD gain for the fingers here; the real Feetech/DaMiao hand gains are set on the servos (see hardware). The tunables below are the RETARGETER cost weights + the pinch/grasp thresholds.

clutch._doc: Double-pinch either hand to FREEZE/recenter the whole body; single pinch is left free for grasping (hysteresis on/off avoids chatter).

hardware._doc: ORCA hand on Feetech STS/SCS servos over TTL serial. Per-servo PD/current limits are set in the servo registers via the firmware GUI (end-stop calibration lives on that bus, not in this file). Fill in the realized servo gains here once the hands are characterized on the robot.

lift._doc: Vertical lift column (cascaded tendon; actuator units [0, 0.635] m). In manipulation mode the lift is NOT part of the fast IK — the lazy follower creeps it to keep the hand centroid near a comfortable height. hw_max_speed is the firmware 60 mm/s ceiling.

hardware._doc: BTS7960 DC motor + quadrature encoder, closed-loop on a Pico over USB serial. The position loop lives on the Pico; max_pos is updated by on-Pico calibration. LIFT enabled=false by default until a Pico is on the port.

torso._doc: Torso pitch hinge (range [-1.047, 0.262] rad; negative = lean forward). The lazy follower leans the body forward for moderate forward reach before the base has to translate.

gravity_feedforward._doc: Trim on the POSTURE-AWARE torso gravity feedforward: tau_ff = scale * tau_mjcf(theta, q_arms) + offset_nm. tau_mjcf is the arm-pose-aware MJCF prediction (arm_control.ArmGravityCompensator with 'torso' in the pose dict, hand mass per HandsConfig); this trim calibrates it onto the real DM-J10422P, fitted by hardware_bridge/experiments/exp_torso_gravity_sysid.py (hold-and-measure sweep at the live arm pose; down-then-up so friction cancels). Read LIVE by controller/mabel/torso_control/gravity.py::ff_trim(). Fitted 2026-07-29 (arms parked, no hands): 13 holds over [-42°, +5°], residual rms 1.99 N·m ~= the stiction band (vs 3.82 for the old sinusoid, 4.16 untrimmed); scale 0.70 matches the arm sysid's l_j2 mass trim 0.72. Re-run at an extended arm pose and refit jointly to pin the arm-dependent term.

hardware._doc: DaMiao DM-J10422P on the arms Teensy CAN bus 3 (backend 'openarm'), MIT mode. Compliant tune 2026-07-29: the posture-aware feedforward carries gravity, PD only tracks + fights friction, so kp drops 150 -> 90. Measured accuracy (settled worst / moving max): kp 60 -> 2.1/4.0 deg, 90 -> 1.2/3.2, 120 -> 0.7/2.7; all smooth. Residual = the +/-2 N.m rest-friction band over kp.

body._doc: The DaMiao 'body' bus groups the torso + 3-DOF neck on one CAN bus (MIT mode, same protocol as the arms). Control-law gains for these joints are the torso/neck blocks above; this block records the shared bus defaults. Configure joint_motors as e.g. 'torso:can0:1, neck_yaw:can0:2, neck_pitch:can0:3, neck_roll:can0:4' and set MABEL_HW_BODY=true to bring it up.
